headline: US and China extend trade truce until Jan 10 as Xi visits Washington
summary: President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping for a three-day visit aimed at easing tensions over trade, technology, and geopolitics.
details: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that Washington and Beijing have reached a deal to extend their trade truce until January 10, moving the previous expiration date of November 10.

The announcement came as President Donald Trump personally greeted Chinese President Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland, marking the first time in 11 years a US president has welcomed a foreign leader at that location.
The visit follows a period of extreme tension, including a 2025 tariff war that saw triple-digit levies between the world's two largest economies.
Despite the trade extension, deep differences remain regarding export controls on computer chips and rare-earth minerals, as well as China's ties with Iran and US support for Taiwan.
President Xi stated in a written release that the two nations should be partners rather than rivals, though he did not explicitly mention the trade deal.
Upcoming discussions are expected to cover potential tariff reductions in specific sectors, cooperation on drug trafficking, and expanded military-to-military dialogue.
The visit also includes a state dinner featuring tech leaders from companies like Apple, Nvidia, and OpenAI to discuss competition and dangers surrounding AI.
Analysts suggest the summit is a scripted effort to project global stability between the world's biggest factory and its biggest consumer, despite conflicting views on the decline of the US economy.
caption:
The world's two largest economies just bought more time. The US and China have extended their trade truce until January 10.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that Washington and Beijing have reached a deal to extend their trade truce until January 10, moving the previous expiration date of November 10.

The announcement came as President Donald Trump personally greeted Chinese President Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland, marking the first time in 11 years a US president has welcomed a foreign leader at that location.

The visit follows a period of extreme tension, including a 2025 tariff war that saw triple-digit levies between the world's two largest economies.

Despite the trade extension, deep differences remain regarding export controls on computer chips and rare-earth minerals, as well as China's ties with Iran and US support for Taiwan.

President Xi stated in a written release that the two nations should be partners rather than rivals, though he did not explicitly mention the trade deal.

Upcoming discussions are expected to cover potential tariff reductions in specific sectors, cooperation on drug trafficking, and expanded military-to-military dialogue.

The visit also includes a state dinner featuring tech leaders from companies like Apple, Nvidia, and OpenAI to discuss competition and dangers surrounding AI.

Analysts suggest the summit is a scripted effort to project global stability between the world's biggest factory and its biggest consumer, despite conflicting views on the decline of the US economy.

headline_marked: Meta [[considering opening Dhaka office]] after high-level talks
headline: Meta considering opening Dhaka office after high-level talks
summary: The tech giant is interested in establishing a local presence in Bangladesh, citing the country's massive Facebook user base.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed announced that Meta is interested in opening an office in Dhaka. The company will review the timing and method of establishing a local presence in Bangladesh.
The announcement came during a press conference at Bangladesh’s Permanent Mission to the UN in New York, following a meeting with Meta representatives during the 81st UN General Assembly session.
According to the state minister, Bangladesh is the eighth-largest Facebook user base globally, with a larger number of users than India, making it a strategic focal point for the company.
The discussions also covered the new Cyber Security Act and ways Meta can collaborate with the government to enhance digital safety and reduce digital harassment.
Meta expressed interest in supporting the expansion of e-commerce and online businesses in Bangladesh, as well as collaborating with educational institutions.
The company's interest aligns with the government's emphasis on e-commerce and technology in the current national budget, which Meta representatives appreciated.
caption:
Bangladesh is the 8th largest Facebook user base in the world. Now, Meta is considering opening an office in Dhaka.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed announced that Meta is interested in opening an office in Dhaka. The company will review the timing and method of establishing a local presence in Bangladesh.

The announcement came during a press conference at Bangladesh’s Permanent Mission to the UN in New York, following a meeting with Meta representatives during the 81st UN General Assembly session.

According to the state minister, Bangladesh is the eighth-largest Facebook user base globally, with a larger number of users than India, making it a strategic focal point for the company.

The discussions also covered the new Cyber Security Act and ways Meta can collaborate with the government to enhance digital safety and reduce digital harassment.

Meta expressed interest in supporting the expansion of e-commerce and online businesses in Bangladesh, as well as collaborating with educational institutions.

The company's interest aligns with the government's emphasis on e-commerce and technology in the current national budget, which Meta representatives appreciated.
